The greatest common divisor of \(n+7\) and \(2n+1\) can be found using the Euclidean algorithm:

\[
\gcd(n+7, 2n+1) = \gcd(n+7, 2n+1 - 2(n+7)) = \gcd(n+7, -13) = \gcd(n+7, 13).
\]

Thus, the gcd must be a divisor of 13, so the possible values are 1 and 13. The maximum possible value is 13, which occurs when \(13 \mid (n+7)\), i.e., \(n \equiv 6 \pmod{13}\). For example, when \(n = 6\), \(n+7 = 13\) and \(2n+1 = 13\), so \(\gcd(13, 13) = 13\).

Answer: 13
